Print, summarize and predict from a fitted emulator

Source: R/emulator_methods.R
spDBL_emulator-methods.Rd

Methods for the result of emulator_learn(). print() shows the model settings. summary() adds the in-sample fit of the smoothed coefficients and the posterior mean of the residual variance. predict() calls emulator_predict(), or with interval = "prediction" returns pointwise predictive distributions.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'spDBL_emulator'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spDBL_emulator'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spDBL_emulator'
predict(
  object,
  newdata,
  dt_pde_test = NULL,
  F_new_ls = "default",
  MC = FALSE,
  interval = c("none", "prediction"),
  level = 0.95,
  ...
)

Arguments

x, object

An spDBL_emulator from emulator_learn().

...

Unused.

newdata

Matrix (or vector, for one run) of new mechanistic inputs.

dt_pde_test, F_new_ls, MC

Passed to emulator_predict().

interval

"none" (the default) returns what emulator_predict() returns. "prediction" returns the pointwise predictive distribution given the autoregressive rows: for each site and time, a Student-t distribution from integrating the coefficients, the residual covariance and the input Gaussian process analytically.

level

Coverage of the central prediction intervals.

Value

print() returns x invisibly. summary() returns an object of class summary.spDBL_emulator, a list with

settings

One-row data frame of model settings.

rmse_by_time

Root mean squared error of the smoothed fit \(F_e \hat\Theta_e\) to the training responses, at each time.

rmse

The same over all times.

response_sd

Standard deviation of the training responses.

residual_variance

Posterior mean of the residual variance, averaged over the sites of a block: \(D/(n-C-1)\) for the inverse-Wishart model and \(D/(n-1)\) times the mean diagonal of R_episode for the \(\sigma^2 R\) model, from the final filter.

predict() returns what emulator_predict() returns, or, with interval = "prediction", a list with time-indexed lists mean, sd, lower and upper of new-run by site matrices (the bounds of central intervals with coverage level), plus level, distribution and the degrees of freedom df.

See also

emulator_learn(), emulator_predict()

Examples

data("dt_emulation")
d <- dt_emulation
em <- emulator_learn(d$pde_para_train, d$dt_pde_train, Nx = 10, Ny = 10,
                     nsam = 5, seed = 1)
em
#> spDBL emulator (inverse-Wishart covariance, marginal coefficient sampling)
#>   Training runs: 40 with 5 inputs
#>   Grid: 10 x 10 (100 sites) over 26 times
#>   Episodes: 260 = 26 times x 10 blocks of 10 sites
#>   Design: AR(2), 20 columns
#>   Stored posterior draws: 5
summary(em)
#> spDBL emulator summary
#>   Covariance: iw; sampling: marginal; AR order: 2
#>   40 runs x 100 sites x 26 times; 260 episodes; 5 stored draws
#>   In-sample RMSE of the smoothed fit: 0.05785 (response SD 3.137)
#>   Posterior mean residual variance per site: 0.003574
pred <- predict(em, d$pde_para_test, dt_pde_test = d$dt_pde_test)
dim(pred[[3]])
#> [1]  10 100
band <- predict(em, d$pde_para_test, dt_pde_test = d$dt_pde_test,
                interval = "prediction")
# Share of held-out outputs at time 3 inside the 95% prediction intervals
mean(d$dt_pde_test[[3]] >= band$lower[[3]] & d$dt_pde_test[[3]] <= band$upper[[3]])
#> [1] 0.918
